children: Our Bureau New Delhi: The road tranport ministry Monday approved E100 or pure ethanol, along with E85, for flex-fuel vehicles, intensifying efforts to further reduce costly fuel imports. In a notification, the ministry said E85 or E100 will be used only in vehicles marked by automakers as flex-fuel. Existing vehicles cannot be tweaked to run on higher blend ethanol fuel beyond E20-a mix of 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.

The government's move comes during a period of volatility in global oil markets due to the West Asia crisis, sharply inflating India's crude import bill. The ministry also changed certain vehicle classification thresholds, fuel specifications, and technical references used in emission-related tables and testing provisions.

This includes raising the vehicle weight limit to 3,500 kg from the previous threshold of 3,000 kg for light petrol and diesel vehicles affected by these changes. This June, Maruti Suzuki launched India's first flex-fuel car, the Wagon R Flex Fuel, capable of running on ethanol-petrol blends from E20 to E100.

Flex-fuel vehicles are designed to run on higher ethanol blends such as E85, a mix of 85% ethanol and 15% petrol, and E100, unlike conventional petrol vehicles currently approved for lower ethanol concentrations. Major automakers including Toyota Motor Corporation, Tata Motors and Hyundai Motor Company are also developing flex-fuel vehicles for the Indian market. The draft changes to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, are aimed at providing for wider use of fuels such as E85 and E100, as well as B100 biodiesel and hydrogen-CNG combination.

title: E100 Gets Nod for Flex-Fuel Vehicles amid Bid to Cut Costly Crude Imports
